title: Cognitive Function in Athletes Cleared for Return-to-Play After Sport-Related Concussion
official: Cognitive Function in Athletes Cleared for Return-to-Play After Sport-Related Concussion (Cog-RTP)
summary: The purpose of this study is to determine whether a brief, objective cognitive assessment can detect exercise-induced changes in cognitive performance in adolescent athletes who have been medically cleared for return-to-play following sport-related concussion.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* 12-18 years old
* Actively engaged in organized sports activities within the past 12 months
* Completed RTP (Return-to-Play) testing within the past 30 days

Exclusion Criteria:

* History of ocular or muscular spasms
* History of epileptic seizures
* History of fainting or loss of consciousness triggered by flashes of light, patterns, or exposure to infrared light sources (e.g., eye tracker)
* History of eye surgery and lenses implanted with different prescriptions in each eye
* History of ptosis (drooping eyelids)
* Taking medications that cause pupil dilation
* Active concussion symptoms
* Cardiovascular, respiratory, or neurological conditions contraindicating exertion
* Orthopedic or neurologic, or other limitations
* History of moderate or severe traumatic brain injury (GCS ≤12)
* Uncontrolled asthma
* Limited English proficiency
